title: TikTok Founder Zhang Yiming Overtakes Mukesh Ambani as Asia's Second-Richest Person
excerpt: ByteDance co-founder's net worth surges to $92.8 billion after a jump in company valuations, pushing Reliance's Ambani to third in Bloomberg's rankings.
body:
• ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming's net worth hit $92.8 billion, surpassing Mukesh Ambani's $86.9 billion on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
  • Bloomberg lowered its risk discount on ByteDance's valuation from 25% to 10% after the completion of TikTok's US business sale and fresh institutional investor filings.
  • ByteDance's Doubao AI chatbot has surpassed 300 million monthly users, becoming China's most popular AI product.
  • Gautam Adani remains Asia's richest person at $117.4 billion, while Ambani has slipped to third.

ByteDance co-founder Zhang Yiming has overtaken Mukesh Ambani to become Asia's second-richest person, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index. The 43-year-old's net worth climbed to $92.8 billion, cementing his position as China's wealthiest individual and pushing the Reliance Industries chairman — long a fixture at the top of Asian wealth rankings — down to third place with a fortune of $86.9 billion.

Gautam Adani retains the top spot among Asian billionaires at $117.4 billion, according to Bloomberg.

A $24 Billion Wealth Jump

Zhang's fortune swelled by more than $24 billion after Bloomberg reassessed ByteDance's valuation using data from several major institutional investors. BlackRock Inc., Fidelity Investments, T. Rowe Price Group Inc., HSG, and General Atlantic all filed updated valuations for the private tech giant in late May.

The index had previously applied a 25% risk discount to ByteDance's valuation following a March 2024 US House of Representatives bill that threatened to ban TikTok unless its Chinese parent sold the app. That discount was lowered to 10% on June 2, reflecting the completion of TikTok's US business transfer to a consortium led by Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX earlier in 2026.

"The jump in valuation reflects the company's strong fundamentals and the success of its apps such as Doubao in China. The developments in the US are unlikely to have a major negative impact."

— Amy Lin, Analyst, Capital Securities (Shanghai)

TikTok and AI Driving Growth

Two forces have powered ByteDance's surging valuation. TikTok remains one of the world's most popular social media platforms, continuing to attract large audiences across global markets even after years of regulatory scrutiny.

But the company's AI ambitions may be the bigger story. ByteDance's Doubao chatbot has amassed more than 300 million monthly active users, making it China's most popular AI product, according to Bloomberg. The company is discussing AI-related expenditures of up to $70 billion in 2026, aiming to challenge leading US players in the space.

Much of that investment is expected to come from ByteDance's roughly $50 billion in profit earned during 2025. The company's global revenue grew 30% last year to approximately $110 billion, according to the Hurun Research Institute.

"Removing the US overhang unlocked the re-rating of the remaining ByteDance entity. Even with the re-rating, the valuation still looks cheap on fundamentals."

— Ke Yan, Analyst, DZT Research (Singapore)

Zhang's Rise From $13 Billion

Zhang Yiming founded ByteDance in 2012, building the company behind the news aggregator Toutiao and the short-video platform Douyin, known internationally as TikTok. He stepped down as CEO in November 2021 but retains more than 50% of ByteDance's voting rights, according to Reuters.

His fortune has grown more than sevenfold since Bloomberg began tracking it in March 2019, when his net worth stood at $13 billion. He first became China's richest person in 2025, was briefly overtaken, and reclaimed the title earlier this year.

What It Means for Ambani and Indian Wealth

Ambani's drop to third place in Asia marks a shift in the continent's wealth hierarchy. For years, the Reliance chairman and Adani have traded positions atop Asian rich lists, with Chinese tech founders lagging behind. Zhang's ascent signals a broader trend: China's AI and tech sector is generating fortunes at a pace that rivals — and now surpasses — India's industrial conglomerates.

Forbes' real-time billionaire list still ranks Ambani as Asia's richest, with a net worth of $89.5 billion, and lists Zhang at $69.3 billion — a reminder that different methodologies produce starkly different rankings. The Bloomberg index, which incorporates private company valuations and institutional filings, tends to be more aggressive in marking up stakes in firms like ByteDance.

What's Next

ByteDance remains a strong candidate for an eventual initial public offering, which could further reshape global wealth rankings. If the company proceeds with its planned $70 billion AI spending push, the outcome will carry implications not just for Zhang's personal fortune but for the competitive landscape between US and Chinese tech.
image_caption: Zhang Yiming, co-founder and chairman of ByteDance, the parent company of TikTok. His net worth climbed to $92.8 billion, making him Asia's second-richest person and surpassing Mukesh Ambani on the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.
nri_angle: The ranking shift underscores the growing challenge Chinese tech fortunes pose to Indian business dynasties, with Reliance's Ambani dropping to third in Asia despite his own empire's expansion.
